summary: self-certificates ships PEM-disguised remote-code-fetch stager that pipes attacker payload into python
details: index.js reads test/key.pem (armored as an RSA PRIVATE KEY), strips the PEM header/footer, base64-decodes the body to recover a JavaScript stager, and passes it as the third argument to selfsign.generate() from the co-published self-sign dependency. The decoded stager fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php (host itself base64-encoded inside the payload) and pipes the response body into a detached python3/python interpreter via stdin, with stdio ignored and windowsHide:true to hide the child process. The path fires whenever a consumer calls the package's exported generateCertificates(), so any application using this library to produce a self-signed certificate executes attacker-controlled Python code fetched from a mutable remote URL. The multi-layer wrapping (fake PRIVATE KEY armor -> base64 -> inner CERTIFICATE armor -> base64 JS -> base64-encoded URL string) is consistent with deliberate concealment from casual review and secret scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
